Composite identity built by string concatenation must be injective
issues.reason: The Durable Object name, so a collision would merge two Actors onto one store. encodeURIComponent percent-escapes the ':' separator, so neither the ActorKind nor the ActorId can introduce one, and the fixed three-segment prefix makes the part count exactly five. parseActorObjectName re-encodes what it decoded and rejects the name unless it is byte-identical, so any non-canonical spelling is refused rather than accepted as an alias.

issues.message: Composite identity built by string concatenation must be injective
issues.reason: Content-addressed storage, so a collision would serve one object for another; it cannot happen here. Both components come from hex(), which emits exactly 64 lowercase hex characters and so can hold no '/', and the sole call site in contentObjectAddress supplies sha256(tenantId.value) and sha256(bytes). Every other segment is a fixed literal, so the key is injective in the pair and cross-tenant reuse would require a SHA-256 collision.

issues.message: Composite identity built by string concatenation must be injective
issues.reason: Grants access to a live Environment Session, so a collision would resolve one session's preview to another; it cannot happen here. The label pair is a positional split at offset 32 of Digest.sha256(...).value, which the Digest constructor pins to 64 lowercase hex, so there is no delimiter to straddle. The digested input is canonical JSON over the full identity -- environmentId, environmentRevision, exposureId, generation, port, sessionEpoch and sessionId -- which is itself injective, and previewHost is construction-time configuration validated against ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9.-]*[a-z0-9])?$, identical for every request. Distinct sessions therefore differ unless SHA-256 collides.

issues.message: Composite identity built by string concatenation must be injective
issues.reason: Not an identity: the result is only interpolated into the refusal message of an unequal-pin merge, and nothing in the system keys, stores, compares, or parses it. The programmatic answer the SPEC requires is the structured RunPinDivergence[] that RunPins.divergence returns, which callers read by dimension and PackageId; recovering the divergence by parsing this string is the message-prose dependency ACQ-ERR and the sqlite duplicate-append fix exist to forbid. A collision here can therefore merge no two records, only render two divergences with the same words.

issues.message: Composite identity built by string concatenation must be injective
issues.reason: derive prefixes a fixed module-constant domain to a SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical JSON of { domain, evidence }. The digest alone binds both components, so the readable prefix cannot create a collision two distinct (domain, evidence) pairs; injectivity is the digest's collision resistance, which ASM-CANONICAL-KEY-INJECTIVE already assumes.
